items.prompt: May the known-sigma normal-mean helper silently replace sigma with a sample standard deviation and claim the same exact finite-sample method?

options.text: Yes, every estimate is equivalent to a known parameter
options.why: Estimated scale changes the sampling distribution.

options.text: Yes, if the printed endpoints have six decimal places
options.why: Formatting precision does not remove statistical uncertainty.

options.text: Yes, for any sample with a positive mean
options.why: The mean sign has no such implication.

options.text: No; estimated scale requires a justified different method
options.why: Under iid normal sampling the t method accounts for this estimated scale.

items.explanation: A known population parameter and a data-derived estimate are different assumptions, even if they happen to have the same numeric value.
